title: alpha-AOS canary catalog
description: Closed-world contract for catalog/canaries.yaml. Every prompt a canary run may put in front of a model is declared here and nowhere else, so rewording one to make a capability pass is a reviewable diff rather than an invisible edit inside a code path. Namespaced x-* extensions are split out before validation, so every object described here is exhaustive.

toolName.description: An UPSTREAM tool name, exactly as the server publishes it. Not a harness-prefixed alias: a harness may present the same tool as mcp__<server>__<tool>, and recording the prefixed form would bind the expectation to one harness's naming convention.

canaries.description: Every declared canary. An empty list is refused: a catalog that silently stopped declaring anything would look exactly like a host on which nothing needed proving.

^x-[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$.description: A namespaced extension. Preserved verbatim and inert; nothing in alpha-AOS reads it. The same rule governs every nested declared object in this repository's catalog contracts — see schemas/pack-catalog.schema.json and schemas/fact-vocabulary.schema.json.

id.description: Stable canary identifier, referenced by ledger rows and by status output.

capability.description: The requirement this canary is evidence for. Narrowed to the requirements this phase declares canaries for, because a canary naming a requirement nobody planned is far more likely to be a typo than a new capability.

prompt.description: The ordinary request handed to the harness. It MUST NOT name the skill, the MCP server or the tool it is meant to elicit — the expectation lists below exist precisely so the prompt does not have to hint. A prompt that only works when it hints is a finding about discovery, not a prompt to revise. Judged by whether a reasonable person reading it would call it an ordinary request.

expectTools.description: Upstream tool names an observation must show. Empty declares a canary whose expectation is about fan-out rather than about any particular tool. Order is significant only when expectOrdered is true.

expectOrdered.description: Whether expectTools must appear in the declared order. Absent means unordered.

expectArgumentPatterns.description: Structural facts an expected call's arguments must satisfy. A structural assertion about the call, never a judgment about the answer the model gave.

argument.description: The argument name on that tool call.

pattern.description: An ECMAScript regular expression source the argument value must match.

why.description: What the pattern proves, in the words a reviewer needs.

forbidTools.description: Tool names whose appearance is a FINDING rather than a failure. Used for the fan-out control and for tools a policy proxy denies: seeing one means the routing contract and the shipped instructions disagree.

maxDistinctServers.description: How many distinct research servers one run of this canary may touch. Written as a COUNT rather than as a required tool sequence, because more than one two-tool path is reasonable — the discovery server itself also ships a fetch tool (03-RESEARCH.md Pitfall 1, second-order note). A control declares 1.

requiresEnvironment.description: Environment variable NAMES this canary needs present. Names only — the readiness probe reads presence and never a value, and the blocked reason it produces has no field able to carry one.

requiresMcpServers.description: MCP server ids that must be CONNECTED before this canary runs. A registered-but-pending server is a registration fact only and does not satisfy this; the harness's own connection listing is the oracle.

harnesses.description: The surfaces this canary is declared for. Narrowed to the harnesses a ledger proof can name: antigravity has no non-interactive entrypoint, so a canary declared for it could never run.

readOnly.description: Whether the canary asks only for read-only work. Declared rather than assumed, and false is not currently permitted: a canary that could mutate the user's repository is not a diagnostic.

why.description: What this canary is evidence FOR, for a reviewer reading the diff rather than the code.
